findings.description: The RDS instance sets publicly_accessible = true, giving the database a public endpoint reachable from the internet rather than keeping it private to the VPC. This dramatically widens the attack surface for a database holding application data.
storage_encrypted = false disables KMS encryption of the RDS volume and its snapshots, leaving stored data unprotected at the storage layer.

The master password is supplied via var.password and the same value is interpolated into EC2 user_data, so the credential is handled as plaintext configuration/state rather than being sourced from Secrets Manager or generated as a managed master password.

The attached parameter group does not set require_secure_transport, and the PHP client connects with mysqli_connect without TLS options, so MySQL traffic to the publicly accessible instance can occur in cleartext.

The user_data script embeds the RDS master username and password into /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc. EC2 user_data is retrievable from the instance metadata service by any process or SSRF-capable web app on the instance, and is also stored unencrypted in the instance description.

No metadata_options block is specified, so IMDSv1 remains available. Combined with the instance profile carrying wildcard s3/ec2/rds permissions, an SSRF in the PHP application could be used to steal role credentials.
No root_block_device with encrypted = true is defined, so the EBS root volume containing the database credential file is stored unencrypted.

The inline policy grants s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* on Resource "*" to the role assumed by the internet-facing web server. This violates least privilege and provides a direct privilege-escalation and data-exfiltration path if the instance or PHP app is compromised.
The database security group permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, allowing a compromised database host to reach arbitrary internet destinations for exfiltration or command and control.
Database access on 3306 is granted to the entire VPC CIDR rather than to the application security group, so any host in the VPC can attempt to authenticate to the database.

findings.issue_category: public IP exposure of web server
findings.description: The instance is placed in a subnet and its public_dns is exported as an output, indicating a public IP is assigned; the attached security group (aws_security_group.portal_sg, defined elsewhere) governs ingress and should be verified to not allow unrestricted access to HTTP/SSH.
